features.t: Resources, methods and integrations (Lambda, HTTP, Mock)
x: AWS_IAM and COGNITO_USER_POOLS authorization types are stored and returned but not enforced; only NONE is evaluated on invoke/test.

features.t: Deploy to a stage; stage variables, throttling, invoke URL
x: The invoke URL is well-formed and the stage's deployed integration chain truly executes (via Test), but the host-based execute-api endpoint isn't reachable by DNS from outside Vyomi — use Test or the CLI/SDK against the appliance's own address.

features.t: Enable CORS (console convenience: adds an OPTIONS mock method + headers)
Account settings (CloudWatch role ARN, account-level throttling)
Usage plans (throttle, quota, API-stage and API-key association)

x: The certificate is a real, uniquely-generated PEM-shaped credential stored and returned by the API, but nothing in Vyomi validates it against an actual mTLS handshake.
$connect/$disconnect/$default routes and Lambda integrations are modeled like HTTP routes; there is no persistent WebSocket connection registry (@connections management API) in Vyomi.

The domain resource, its endpoint configuration and API mappings are stored and returned exactly as configured, but no certificate validation or DNS provisioning happens — there is no real ACM/Route 53 behind it.

features.t: Domain name access associations (VPC endpoint ↔ private custom domain)

x: VpcLinkStatus always reports AVAILABLE; Vyomi has no real NLB/VPC to actually attach to.

features.t: AgentCore targets (MCP access via Bedrock AgentCore)
x: Lists and manages the targets of Vyomi AgentCore gateways (see bedrock.agentcore.gateway): Lambda targets are real MCP tools; other target kinds are registered only.

Publishing a portal (PublishPortal) flips publishStatus to PUBLISHED and the portal/preview URLs are well-formed, but — like the execute-api invoke host — they aren't reachable by DNS from outside Vyomi; there is no real Cognito user pool behind a Cognito-authorized portal.

CreateDeployment(canarySettings), CreateStage/UpdateStage canarySettings (percentTraffic, stageVariableOverrides, useStageCache, promote via deploymentId, delete) are real: each request is routed to the canary with probability percentTraffic and then sees the canary's stage-variable overrides and deployment id, and stage variables are substituted into the integration URI (${stageVariables.name}) and reach Lambda. Deployments are not snapshots of the API configuration here, so stable and canary share the current resources/methods/integrations and differ only by stage variables and deployment id; useStageCache has no effect (stage caching is not modeled).
